meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Time: 09:45 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Peregrine CTO), Priya Patel (Lead ML Engineer), Alex Chen (SRE), Dana Lee (PM)
Recording: https://redwood.zoom/rec/ff-20260730-peregrine (note: link placeholder)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Peregrine Labs team through migration parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Focus areas: API parity (function calling, streaming, structured output), tokenization differences, latency/cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and next steps to run benchmarks and share configs.
topics: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, VPC/private deployments
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um Miguel, Priya, Alex, Dana, hi. We're gonna run through a migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood, focus on parity mapping and ops.
[00:14] Miguel Torres: Yep thanks Jordan, quick context: we've got prod usage on OpenAI and some Anthro-pic for safety prompts, and we're experimenting with Together for cost. Main concerns: latency, token differences, and security for our regulated data.
[00:28] Samira Khan: Great, we'll show the API surface first, then the console and Optimize suggestions. Quick note: some automatic transcripts may say "K-V cache" or "K V cache" - we mean KV cache.
[01:05] Priya Patel: One thing up front - function calling compatibility is big for us. Our dialog system depends on tool calls and structured responses. How closely does Redwood match OpenAI's function call schema?
[01:19] Samira Khan: Function calling is supported; payloads are the same shape, you can pass schema and Redwood will return structured JSON. We do have small differences in the streaming chunks metadata - we can share a mapping. For 95% of apps it's drop-in, for edge cases we'll show an example.
[02:02] Alex Chen: And tokenizer behavior? We've seen tokenization shifts when moving models which affects cost.
[02:10] Samira Khan: Good question. Redwood exposes model-specific tokenizers and provides a tokenization preview endpoint; we also include a parity sheet mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together model tokens to Redwood model equivalents. The parity mapping we'll send includes typical deltas and recommended model picks (e.g., text-davinci-ish -> redwood-large-v1, claude-like -> redwood-steadfast-v1).
[03:00] Jordan Park: Let's jump into a live demo. Samira, can you share your screen?
[03:15] Samira Khan: Sharing now - ok console view. Top left is model catalog, you can filter by latency/cost/arch. Here is an example mapping we created for Peregrine: OpenAI gpt-4o -> redwood-ignite-4o (approx), Anthropic Claude-2 -> redwood-steadfast-claude-compat, Together T-70 -> redwood-economy-t70-quant.
[04:02] Miguel Torres: When you say "approx" what's the guarantee? We need to know quality regressions will be flagged.
[04:12] Samira Khan: We recommend running a small eval set - Redwood Optimize can run quality regressions tied to a prompt set and alert you. For migrations we do a side-by-side diff on outputs, and our console shows quality delta and token delta per example.
[04:45] Priya Patel: How about batch inference and throughput? We have high-throughput embedding and chat workloads.
[04:52] Samira Khan: Two levers: batching and KV cache. For chat, prefix caching avoids re-sending system prompts; batch sizing is configurable per model and we give recommended profiles per workload in Optimize. Dedicated capacity lets you guarantee throughput; hosted has autoscaling with burst options.
[05:28] Alex Chen: Security - does Redwood support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
[05:33] Jordan Park: Yep - Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC-only endpoints. We also have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs available as part of our Enterprise pack. We'll attach the security pack after the call.
[06:02] Dana Lee: Can you show an example of model rollback / canary?
[06:10] Samira Khan: Sure - here's a rollout config. You can set a canary at 5%, auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant, or route by latency SLO. The console shows per-route tokens, latency percentiles, and traces.
[06:45] Jordan Park: Back to API parity - here's a sample request that emulates OpenAI's chat completions / function calling.
[06:52] Samira Khan: [reads code] POST /v1/responses with model=redwood-ignite-4o, messages, functions, function_call=auto. The response body returns content and an optional function_call object. There's an extra top-level field we add for streaming metadata (partial_token_offset) - small clients can ignore it.
[07:30] Miguel Torres: Any runway for code changes on our side? We want minimal work.
[07:36] Samira Khan: For most teams it's minimal - usually just update the endpoint and model names, and run a tokenization check. We'll provide the parity map + a small compatibility shim you can drop into your client to normalize streaming events.
[08:05] Priya Patel: About cost - do you have direct per-token pricing and how do you suggest quantization?
[08:13] Jordan Park: Pricing depends on hosted vs dedicated. For migration, Optimize will recommend quant settings (int8/int4) per model and expected quality impact. For embeddings and high-volume generation you often save 30-60% with quant+batching. We'll provide a cost model example.
[09:00] Samira Khan: Now demoing the Optimize tab - here's a workload profile we simulated with Peregrine's expected 100k requests/day. It suggests: 1) enable prefix caching for chat, 2) use redwood-economy-t70 with int8 for non-critical summarization, 3) reserve a small Dedicated pool for peak hours.
[09:40] Alex Chen: For Dedicated, what's the SLA?
[09:44] Jordan Park: Typically 99.9% uptime and tail latency SLOs depending on pool size - we can get contractual numbers in the pricing doc.
[10:05] Miguel Torres: Let's talk about telemetry and cost breakdowns. We need per-route token-level costs and per-request latency breakdown.
[10:13] Samira Khan: Console provides token-level cost, per-model breakdown, and per-route percentiles. We also have tracing hooks to attach request IDs to your observability pipeline.
[11:00] Priya Patel: A couple of tricky areas: 1) streaming and connecting to our websocket gateway, 2) rate-limiting behavior during bursts - how graceful is fallback?
[11:12] Samira Khan: We support streaming over websockets and HTTP chunked. For bursts, routing policies can fallback to a cheaper compatible model or to a separate pool. You can set graceful rejections and queue sizes. We'll include recommended defaults.
[11:45] Dana Lee: Any migration gotchas you've seen?
[11:50] Jordan Park: Tokenization differences (cost changes), function call edge cases, and subtle detokenization differences in structured outputs. Also embedding vector dimension mismatches if you move between providers - we recommend running an embedding stability test.
[12:20] Miguel Torres: Can Samira show a short live parity example - same prompt to OpenAI and Redwood?
[12:25] Samira Khan: Yes - I'll run a side-by-side. Running OpenAI (local mock) -> output A, now Redwood -> output B. You can see differences in phrasing; Optimize flags 0.8 BLEU-ish (note: not exact metric) and suggests a different model or prompt-tuning to match tone.
[14:40] Priya Patel: The transcript quality on previous demos sometimes garbles names - no worries.
[14:47] Samira Khan: Noted. We'll attach a written parity doc.
[15:10] Alex Chen: Regarding function calling, what about large tool payloads? We pass big JSON in arguments.
[15:20] Samira Khan: We recommend using blob storage refs for very large payloads and passing a pointer to the model; function_call supports arbitrary strings but payload size affects token cost.
[15:50] Miguel Torres: Any limits on streaming throughput per connection?
[15:55] Samira Khan: There are connection-level limits, but we support multiplexing across connections. For Dedicated you can set higher per-connection throughput.
[16:30] Jordan Park: Ok switching to security briefly - Priya, Alex, what compliance items do you want upfront?
[16:38] Priya Patel: SOC2 Type II evidence, KMS integration patterns, data residency options, and audit log formats.
[16:45] Jordan Park: We'll send the SOC2 pack and a KMS integration guide. Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and VPC endpoints, and we can run an on-prem package if needed.
[17:10] Dana Lee: Do you support per-customer subnet isolation in Private?
[17:14] Samira Khan: Yes - per-customer VPC with peered control plane (or full on-prem). We'll add architecture diagrams.
[17:40] Miguel Torres: Let's outline a PoC: 1) Parity mapping + config, 2) run 10k prompt benchmark for quality & latency, 3) cost modeling, 4) decision. Timeline? We want results before end of next month.
[17:55] Jordan Park: That sounds right - we can target initial benchmarks within 2 weeks if you provision the prompt samples.
[18:12] Priya Patel: We'll share the prompts and current logs by Aug 1.
[18:20] Jordan Park: Great. Samira, can you capture the benchmark plan?
[18:24] Samira Khan: Yes - plan: use your 1k seed prompts, split for chat/generation/embedding, run side-by-side on OpenAI/Anthropic/Together vs Redwood hosted and a small Dedicated pool. We'll collect latency p95/p99, token delta, and quality diff. Samira to run bench and share commands.
[19:02] Alex Chen: What's the expected infra to run the bench? Do you need SSH to our environment?
[19:09] Samira Khan: No SSH required. We'll provide a test harness (script + Docker) - you run it or we can run against a demo account. If you want on-prem tests, we may coordinate with your SRE for a short window.
[19:38] Miguel Torres: Ok. A few clarifying Qs: 1) Does Redwood support streaming function call partials? 2) Is there a difference in randomness/temperature semantics?
[19:46] Samira Khan: 1) Yes streaming partials for function calls are supported, but the order of events may differ slightly from OpenAI; our shim normalizes it. 2) Temperature semantics are consistent; any small differences are due to model sampling and tokenization.
[20:20] Jordan Park: We should also highlight integration helpers - SDKs for Node/Python, and a small middleware shim for Express/Flask to intercept streaming and function calls.
[20:35] Priya Patel: Will you share the SDK link?
[20:37] Jordan Park: Yes, we'll attach the SDK repo and the sample shim in the follow-up.
[21:00] Samira Khan: One more note on embeddings: if you change encoder families you'll see vector dimension changes. Redwood supports migration helpers that map older vectors to new dimensionality using a reprojection step if needed.
[21:30] Alex Chen: Great. On monitoring, can we export raw request logs for our SIEM?
[21:36] Samira Khan: Yes - audit logs and request-level traces can be exported via S3/HTTPS to your SIEM with configurable retention.
[22:10] Miguel Torres: Any customer references with similar migrations?
[22:14] Jordan Park: We have a fintech and a healthcare customer who moved from OpenAI + Together to Redwood - we'll share high-level case studies (anonymized) showing cost reductions and stability improvements.
[22:40] Priya Patel: Back to cost: can you provide an example TCO for our workload?
[22:45] Jordan Park: We'll run a short TCO model after you share usage logs - that'll be part of the next deliverable.
[23:10] Dana Lee: Anything about legal/contracting? We will likely need a data processing addendum.
[23:16] Jordan Park: Yes, enterprise deals include DPA and add-ons for retention. We'll loop legal once you indicate interest.
[23:45] Miguel Torres: Quick note - when you say "redwood-ignite-4o" is that exact name we should use in code?
[23:52] Samira Khan: For hosted yes; for Dedicated there may be a replica name. We'll standardize names in the parity spreadsheet.
[24:12] Priya Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[24:15] Jordan Park: Recap: 1) Jordan sends parity mapping + security docs, 2) Priya uploads prompt set by Aug 1, 3) Samira schedules benchmark and runs side-by-side, 4) Jordan shares pricing and Dedicated options. Any blockers?
[24:35] Miguel Torres: None on our side, just internal SRE availability for a bench window.
[24:42] Alex Chen: We'll coordinate.
[24:50] Dana Lee: Could we get a one-page summary for our Execs?
[24:53] Jordan Park: Yes, we'll provide a 1-pager with TL;DR results and next steps.
[25:05] Samira Khan: I'll add concrete command lines for the test harness in the follow-up.
[25:20] Miguel Torres: Cool. Two minor follow-ups: if we need function-level determinism testing, who owns that?
[25:28] Samira Khan: We'll support test design; you run with your secret configs. We can help interpret results.
[25:40] Jordan Park: Alright - thanks everyone. We'll send a summarized email after the call with attachments.
[25:48] Miguel Torres: Thanks Jordan, Samira.
[25:52] Priya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[25:55] Alex Chen: Bye.
[25:57] Dana Lee: Thanks, bye.

Note: The above transcript is excerpted to capture key moments; full recording contains Q&A and longer demo steps. Some transcription errors expected (model names, acronyms).
